diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU laser is degrading: TX bias current has risen steadily from approximately 11.6 mA to 14.9 mA, exceeding the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, while RX remains broadly stable in the normal band and the ONU remains online. The falling TX power is still within the calibrated normal range but supports deterioration of the optical transmitter.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully, reports online:1, and has valid authentication, so the customer is not currently offline.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and its OID subtree; CPU, memory, and temperature are normal, ruling out an OLT or router fault.
All visible peers on EPON0/7 are online with normal or strong RX levels, so there is no shared splitter or PON-port issue.
The customer's RX telemetry stays near -24 dBm, within the normal -20 to -25 dBm band, with no decline into degraded range; this does not support fiber degradation.
Distance remains constant at 241, so there is no fibre-path or record step change.
TX power remains within the calibrated normal 0 to +5 dBm range, while TX bias rises from about 11.6 mA to about 14.9 mA and exceeds the healthy maximum.
Rising bias with stable RX is the discriminator for laser degradation and indicates the laser is requiring increasing drive current.
The customer has 6 sessions in 24 hours, below the 8-session flapping threshold, and the authentication record, VLAN 1107, and RADIUS state are consistent.

remediation.action: Replace or swap the subscriber ONU/optical transmitter, then verify RX power, TX power, TX bias current, and session stability. Continue monitoring the line until replacement; do not replace shared PON equipment because all tested peers and the OLT are healthy.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU transmit laser is at end of life. Bias current has risen from 11.4 to 15.1 mA and, over the last two days, output power has begun to fall despite it, meaning compensation is now failing.
expected_reasoning: The customer reports progressive worsening, which fits both fibre degradation and laser degradation
RX sits at -23.9 dBm in the low-normal band and is noisier than the usual floor, but it is flat with no downward trend
TX bias current has climbed from 11.4 to 15.1 mA, well past the 13.0 mA ceiling
TX power held at 2.42 dBm while bias rose, then began falling to 2.05 dBm in the last two days
Falling output despite maximum bias means the laser can no longer compensate
Supply voltage has drifted from 3.45 to 3.36 V, consistent with a failing transmitter
Distance is constant, so there has been no change to the fibre path
Peers on EPON0/7 are normal, so shared infrastructure is not involved
Flat RX with collapsing TX is a transmitter fault, not path attenuation
distractors: RX in the low-normal band with extra noise invites a fibre degradation diagnosis
Steadily declining traffic fits either fault equally well
The complaint wording matches the fibre degradation pattern almost exactly
